what: M55 Phases 28-29 — alerts wired into a runnable checker and PROVEN to fire
tool: tools/ops/realtime_alerts.py — scans the runtime's structured log + probes readiness; one ALERT line per firing condition, exit 1; wire into cron/CI/any ops channel that runs commands

thresholds.stall: hot_decode max > 15 s (the M54 stall signature)
thresholds.not_ready: readiness endpoint unreachable or status != ready

fire_test: forced log with a 16.8 s stall, a trimmed repetition, a dead backend, 5 decode failures, and a 6 s punctuation: ALL FIVE alerts fired, exit 1
silence_test: clean log with normal sessions (fast-path finals included): OK, exit 0 — and normal user cancellation writes NO signature at all, so it can never alert
live_readiness: against the running realtime runtime: OK, exit 0; the backend-down live case is exercised in the failure drill (failure-recovery.json)
production_wiring_note: production runs this on the GPU host on a 1-minute schedule against the runtime log + readiness URL; the ops channel is whatever runs commands (cron+mail, CI, or the future dashboard) — no new infrastructure invented here
